candidates.topic: Low-protein diet and lifespan — rising longevity research signal
candidates.primary_entity: Low-protein diet / dietary protein restriction / longevity

candidates.why_now: 'low protein diet lifespan research' is rising Google Trends query (diet category). Topic intersects genuine scientific debate: protein restriction/mTOR longevity research (Valter Longo, Morgan Levine) vs. high-protein guidance for muscle preservation in aging (current mainstream). Contradiction is genuine tension readers want resolved.
candidates.primary_headline: Could Eating Less Protein Help You Live Longer? The Science Is More Complicated Than You Think
candidates.next_steps: Locate specific new study driving current search query before publishing. Retrieve key prior studies (Cell Metabolism — Levine et al.). Include protein guidance for older adults (sarcopenia prevention) as counterpoint. Do NOT frame as 'eat less protein.'
candidates.notes: Most protein restriction lifespan data from animal models — human applicability uncertain. Direct tension with high-protein guidance for older adults — both sides must be represented. Do not frame conclusion as 'eat less protein' — evidence genuinely context-dependent and complex.
